solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In which magician keeps everything up his sleeve?

definitions.text: In which magician keeps everything up his sleeve?

parts.words: In which magician keeps everything up his sleeve
parts.note: a conjuror's stock of tricks pictured as a sack he keeps them all in, with the phrase also meaning any set of clever ploys

explanation.surface: A question about where a conjuror stores the secrets he hides up his sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: The question is answered literally: the container holding a magician's whole repertoire of illusions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a full repertoire of clever ploys, literally a magician's sack of illusions.

clue.text: Support wretched surrender

parts.note: to back is to support
feeling down is feeling wretched

explanation.surface: Backing a miserable capitulation.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield in an argument or retreat from a position is to give in.

clue.text: Fine getting into pretty yellow carp

indicators.note: entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: fairly gold-coloured
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A fine, fairly yellow carp in a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' is the noun for the fish, not the verb meaning to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: The ornamental pet fish is a member of the carp family.

clue.text: Lie about strength of character

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Lying about how strong a person's character is.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral fibre is toughness and resolve, the backbone of a person.

clue.text: Sceptre could be an emblem to ——-

definitions.text: Sceptre could be an emblem to ——-

indicators.note: says the letters of the preceding word might form another word

explanation.surface: A royal sceptre as a symbol inviting due deference.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is filled by the answer: a sceptre is an emblem commanding esteem, and its letters rearranged spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre symbolises authority that commands esteem and deference.

clue.text: Confused getting cuppa on the slate finally refused

parts.note: cha is slang for tea, a cuppa

indicators.note: the last letters are rejected, here the ends of both words

parts.note: on credit, which in British slang is on tick

explanation.surface: A muddled customer asking for tea on credit and finally being turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally refused' drops the last letter of each of ON and TICK, giving OTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaotic means disordered and in confusion.

clue.text: Private playing — stick at it

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier
a show that is on is playing

explanation.surface: A private keeps going while playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere doggedly despite difficulty, like a soldier marching on.

clue.text: Fellow starts to lie up getting this

definitions.text: Fellow starts to lie up getting this

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words that follow are taken

explanation.surface: A man takes to his bed when he catches something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a fellow who has to lie up has caught this.
explanation.definitionFit: Influenza is the illness that sends a person to bed for a few days.

clue.text: Uproar about brothers boxing

indicators.note: enclosing, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: Fra is the title of a friar, plural Fras
CA is circa, about

explanation.surface: A rumpus over brothers getting into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' suggests fighting but here means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy disturbance or brawl.

clue.text: The cost of care on high part of castle

parts.note: up means aloft
the keep is a castle's central tower

explanation.surface: Maintenance costs for the upper section of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the expense of maintaining something in good repair.

clue.text: Jellied eel consumed by radio star

indicators.note: eaten up by, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: CB is citizens' band radio

indicators.note: set into a new form, so the letters of eel are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broadcaster tucks into a London favourite, jellied eels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jellied' looks like part of the dish's name but is the anagram signal; jellied eels are a traditional East London food.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeb is a celebrity, a famous person or star.

clue.text: Where shoppers go in hunt for rabbit

indicators.note: placed inside the other piece

parts.note: to stalk is to hunt prey stealthily
a shopping mall

explanation.surface: Shoppers heading somewhere while out hunting a rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' here is British slang for chatter (from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' = talk), not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit is to chatter on aimlessly, and idle chatter is light conversation.

clue.text: Rare Fender, if electric, beginning to tempt

indicators.note: charged or excited, so the letters are thrown into a new order
the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A rare Fender electric guitar starts to tempt a collector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electric' looks like it describes the Fender guitar but rearranges FENDERIF; T from 'beginning to tempt' is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is unusual, out of the ordinary, unlike the rest.

clue.text: No quiet in crib — that makes you furious

indicators.note: says the following letter is to be left out

parts.note: to crib is to copy illicitly, as does one who pirates work
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A baby crib with no peace and quiet is enough to make anyone livid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crib' suggests a cot but means copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious and irate are synonyms for very angry.

clue.text: Flop with a cheer

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of encouragement

explanation.surface: A show bombs yet still gets a cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete failure, such as a match ruined by rain, is a flop.

clue.text: Mindful of old boy and batman?

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil
an officer's personal servant in the British army

explanation.surface: Attentive to a former pupil and to Batman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batman' is not the superhero but a soldier who serves an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant and mindful both describe being alert and attentive.

clue.text: Kipper caught close to Yorks river

indicators.note: next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A smoked fish landed near a Yorkshire river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kipper' is the verb: to kipper is to preserve fish by smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: Kippering is a way of preserving fish, so to kipper is to cure by smoking.

clue.text: Slowly is how to count coins

definitions.meaning: gradually, a little at a time
a bit is an old name for a small coin, as in threepenny bit, so they are counted one at a time

explanation.surface: Counting coins one by one takes a while.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means gradually, and literally counting one small coin after another.

clue.text: Timetable is free and clear

indicators.note: the letters are released to form a new order

explanation.surface: A schedule that is open and uncluttered.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is a schedule of dates and events.

clue.text: Regularly popped pills, say, and regularly unsteady

indicators.note: every other letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone habitually taking pills and often wobbly on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Regularly' belongs to the definition; the second one picks the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of 'unsteady'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug user is said to have 'used', taking substances habitually.

clue.text: State and International Court in appointment

indicators.note: placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: A nation and the International Court arranging a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun for a country but is the verb, to say aloud for writing down.
explanation.definitionFit: To dictate is to state words for another to record, or to lay down.

clue.text: Drop girl in Spanish bar

parts.note: to can something is to drop or scrap it
Tina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl being dropped off at a bar in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantina is a bar or tavern in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Come to terms with prisoner and nurse being together

parts.note: con is short for convict
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A prisoner and nurse reconciling in each other's company.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend with something is to grapple with and cope with it.

clue.text: Order in support of rug

parts.note: being for something is supporting it
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: Ordering a rug in favour of something else.
explanation.definitionFit: A format is a layout or arrangement, the order of things.

clue.text: Little fat lad's revolutionary problem

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary
the rub is the problem, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A chubby boy has a problem with rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby winged infants in paintings are plump little boys.

clue.text: Remaining to the right, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something left over, leaning somewhat to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: The remaining ones are the rest, those still left.

clue.text: Busy oil-worker, perhaps

definitions.meaning: British slang for a police officer
John ..., the English landscape painter who worked in oils

explanation.surface: A hard-working employee on an oil rig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' is old British slang for a police officer, and 'oil-worker' is a painter in oils, not a rig hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer of basic rank, and the surname of a celebrated English painter in oils.

clue.text: Short High Street time's forgotten

indicators.note: drunk or intoxicated, so the letters reel into a new order
left out, so the given letter is removed from the mix

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A brief note that the time on the High Street has been forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High Street' is a red herring as a phrase: 'High' rearranges STREET once 'forgotten' takes out a T.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief and curt, using few words.

clue.text: Preserve lame drama for a change

indicators.note: the letters are to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Keeping a weak play going just for variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A preserve is a jam-like spread; this is the citrus kind.

clue.text: Charge involves book burning

indicators.note: takes in, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a raid is a sudden charge or attack

explanation.surface: An accusation in court that involves burning books.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning zeal can be described as fanatical, extreme and furious.

clue.text: Bill thanks Ben in the first instance

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the name is used

explanation.surface: A bill arrives and Ben is thanked first.
explanation.definitionFit: A tab is a bill or running account, as at a bar.

clue.text: Puzzler following fashion — or not in this case

definitions.text: Puzzler following fashion — or not in this case

indicators.note: comes after, so this piece goes second

parts.note: a trend is a current fashion
a crossword setter sets puzzles

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler who follows fashion, or rather does the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the puzzler comes after the fashion; read plainly, such a person leads fashion rather than following it, hence 'or not'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who leads rather than follows fashion is an initiator of new styles.
